premises: Elemental Cr coatings on Zr-alloy cladding fail prematurely at high temperature due to Cr–Zr interdiffusion.
Silicon addition to Cr can form a chromium silicide phase at the Cr–Zr interface.
A chromium silicide interlayer acts as a diffusion barrier, inhibiting Cr–Zr interdiffusion.
The silicide interlayer improves oxidation resistance by contributing to protective scale formation.
The Cr–Si coating will perform well in both subcritical water and high-temperature steam.
